#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 16 -t 24h --setattr=system.memory=128GB --job-name=pico --output=pico.out.{id} --error=pico.err.{id} script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from exclusive + single task)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from -n 1)
# -c 16        : 16 cores per task (from -c 16)
# -t 24h       : 24 hour walltime (from -t 24:00:00)
# --setattr=system.memory=128GB : Total memory ~128GB (16 cores × 8182MB ≈ 128GB)
# --job-name=pico : job name (from -J pico)
# --output=    : stdout redirection (from -o ./pico.out.%j)
# --error=     : stderr redirection (from -e ./pico.err.%j)
#
# Note: Flux uses {id} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: Memory calculation: 16 cores × 8182 MB/core = ~128 GB total
# Adjust memory specification syntax based on your Flux version

# Original job name: pico
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=pico ...

# Original output/error files: ./pico.out.%j and ./pico.err.%j
# Set at submission with job ID placeholder

# Email notification: simpson@ukp.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de (FAIL events only)
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts
# Consider using flux job attach with notifications or external monitoring tools

# Exclusive node access:
# Original: --exclusive flag for exclusive node allocation
# Note: Flux handles exclusivity differently through resource allocation
# By requesting all cores on a node (-c 16 if node has 16 cores), you effectively
# get exclusive access. Alternatively, use node-exclusive scheduling policies
# Performance impact: Without explicit exclusive flag, other jobs might share the node
# if not all resources are requested. Ensure -c matches the node's total core count
# or use Flux scheduling policies for exclusive allocation

# CPU Feature constraint: avx
# Original: -C avx (constraint for AVX instruction set)
# Note: Flux supports node property matching through resource graph properties
# This requires site-specific configuration of node properties in Flux
# Submit with: flux batch --requires="avx" (if configured) or use resource query
# Performance impact: Without AVX constraint, job may be scheduled on nodes without
# AVX support, potentially causing runtime failures or reduced performance
# Consult site-specific Flux documentation for available node properties/constraints
# Alternative: Use flux resource list to identify nodes with AVX and target explicitly

# Memory per CPU: 8182 MB
# Note: Original specifies --mem-per-cpu=8182 (MB)
# Total memory: 16 cores × 8182 MB = ~130,912 MB ≈ 128 GB
# Flux memory specification may use --setattr=system.memory=130912MB
# or --setattr=system.memory=128GB depending on version
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# ----------------------------------

module load intel python/3.6.8
python -u ./src/run_pico_experiments.py

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

Memory calculation discrepancy: The documentation states '16 cores × 8182MB ≈ 128GB' but actual calculation is 16 × 8182 = 130,912 MB ≈ 127.8 GB. The submission command uses '--setattr=system.memory=128GB' which is close but not exact. Consider using '--setattr=system.memory=130912MB' for precision.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=128GB' may not be correct for all Flux versions. Flux typically uses '--setattr=system.memory=131072M' or similar MB-based specifications. The 'GB' suffix may not be universally supported. Verify with local Flux documentation.

The output/error file path uses '{id}' placeholder, but the correct Flux syntax varies by version. Some versions use '{{id}}', '{{jobid}}', or '%j' style formatting. Verify the correct placeholder syntax for your Flux version.

The AVX constraint is documented but not included in the recommended submission command. If AVX is required, the submission command should include '--requires=avx' or equivalent site-specific constraint syntax.

Exclusive node access strategy assumes the node has exactly 16 cores. If nodes have more cores, requesting '-c 16' will NOT provide exclusive access. Consider using '-N 1 --exclusive' if Flux supports it, or explicitly request all node cores.

The recommended submission command should be updated to include the AVX constraint if it's critical: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 16 -t 24h --setattr=system.memory=130912M --requires=avx --job-name=pico --output=pico.out.{{id}} --error=pico.err.{{id}} script.sh'
No validation exists in the script to verify that the required resources (16 cores, 128GB memory, AVX support) are actually available before running the Python script.
The script assumes module environment is compatible with Flux. The 'module load' commands should work, but verify that the module system is properly configured in the Flux environment.
Consider adding resource verification commands at the start of the script, such as checking available cores with 'nproc' or 'lscpu' to confirm the allocation matches expectations.

#SBATCH -t 24:00:00
#SBATCH -J pico
#SBATCH --mail-user=simpson@ukp.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de
#SBATCH --mail-type=FAIL
#SBATCH -e ./pico.err.%j
#SBATCH -o ./pico.out.%j
#SBATCH -n 1
#SBATCH -c 16
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=8182
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -C avx

# ----------------------------------


module load intel python/3.6.8
python -u ./src/run_pico_experiments.py
